parts.text: 请分别调用 webfetch 读取这三个资料地址：https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#examples 、https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#technical_summary 和 https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#:~:text=The%20%3Cdetails%3E%20HTML%20element%20creates%20a%20disclosure%20widget%20in%20which%20information%20is%20visible%20only%20when%20the%20widget%20is%20toggled%20into%20an%20open%20state.%20A%20summary%20or%20label%20must%20be%20provided%20using%20the%20%3Csummary%3E%20element.%20A%20disclosure%20widget%20is%20typically%20presented%20onscreen%20using%20a%20small%20triangle%20that%20rotates%20%28or%20twists%29%20to%20indicate%20open%2Fclosed%20state%2C%20with%20a%20label%20next%20to%20the%20triangle. ，然后用一句话总结资料。不要额外搜索、写文件、创建任务或委托。

parts.text: MDN 资料说明，`<details>` 与 `<summary>` 配合创建默认折叠、展开后显示内容的原生交互组件，可通过 `open` 属性默认展开、相同 `name` 实现互斥手风琴并用 CSS 定制外观（[示例](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#examples)），其内容结构为一个 `<summary>` 后接流内容，起止标签均不可省略，隐式 ARIA 角色为 `group`，DOM 接口为 `HTMLDetailsElement`（[技术摘要](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#technical_summary)）。

` HTML details disclosure element Baseline Widely available \* This feature is well established and works across many devices and browser versions. It’s been available across browsers since January 2020. \* Some parts of this feature may have varying levels of support. - [See full compatibility](#browser_compatibility) - [Learn more](/en-US/docs/Glossary/Baseline/Compatibility) The **`
`** [HTML](/en-US/docs/Web/HTML) element creates a disclosure widget in which information is visible only when the widget is toggled into an open state. A summary or label must be provided using the [``](/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/summary) element. A disclosure widget is typically presented onscreen using a small triangle that rotates (or twists) to indicate open/closed state, with a label next to the triangle. The contents of the `` element are used as the label for the disclosure widget. The contents of the `
` provide the [accessible description](/en-US/docs/Glossary/Accessible_description) for the ``. ## In this article - [Try it](#try_it) - [Attributes](#attributes) - [Usage notes](#usage_notes) - [Examples](#examples) - [Technical summary](#technical_summary) - [Specifications](#specifications) - [Browser compatibility](#browser_compatibility) - [See also](#see_also) ## [Try it](#try_it) ```
Details Something small enough to escape casual notice.
``` ``` details { border: 1px solid #aaaaaa; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.5em 0.5em 0; } summary { font-weight: bold; margin: -0.5em -0.5em 0; padding: 0.5em; } details[open] { padding: 0.5em; } details[open] summary { border-bottom: 1px solid #aaaaaa; margin-bottom: 0.5em; } ``` ## [Attributes](#attributes) This element includes the [global attributes](/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes). [`open`](#open) This Boolean attribute indicates whether the details — that is, the contents of the `
` element — are currently visible. The details are shown when this attribute exists, or hidden when this attribute is absent. By default this attribute is absent which means the details are not visible. **Note:** You have to remove this attribute entirely to make the details hidden. `open="false"` makes the details visible because this attribute is Boolean. [`name`](#name) This attribute enables multiple `
` elements to be connected, with only one open at a time. This allows developers to easily create UI features such as accordions without scripting. The `name` attribute specifies a group name — give multiple `
` elements the same `name` value to group them. Only one of the grouped `
` elements can be open at a time — opening one will cause another to close. If multiple grouped `
` elements are given the `open` attribute, only the first one in the source order will be rendered open. **Note:** `
` elements don't have to be adjacent to one another in the source to be part of the same group. ## [Usage notes](#usage_notes) A `
` widget can be in one of two states. The default *closed* state displays only the triangle and the label inside `` (or a [user agent](/en-US/docs/Glossary/User_agent)\-defined default string if no ``). When the user clicks on the widget or focuses it then presses the space bar, it "twists" open, revealing its contents. The common use of a triangle which rotates or twists around to represent opening or closing the widget is why these are sometimes called "twisty". You can use CSS to style the disclosure widget, and you can programmatically open and close the widget by setting/removing its [`open`](#open) attribute. Unfortunately, at this time, there's no built-in way to animate the transition between open and closed. By default when closed, the widget is only tall enough to display the disclosure triangle and summary. When open, it expands to display the details contained within. Fully standards-compliant implementations automatically apply the CSS ``[`display`](/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/display): list-item`` to the [``](/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/summary) element. You can use this or the [`::marker`](/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Selectors/::marker) pseudo-element to [customize the disclosure widget](/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/summary#changing_the_summarys_icon). ### [Events](#events) In addition to the usual events supported by HTML elements, the `
` element supports the [`toggle`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/toggle_event "toggle") event, which is dispatched to the `
` element whenever its state changes between open and closed. It is sent *after* the state is changed, although if the state changes multiple times before the browser can dispatch the event, the events are coalesced so that only one is sent. You can use an event listener for the `toggle` event to detect when the widget changes state: js ``` details.addEventListener("toggle", (event) => { if (details.open) { /* the element was toggled open */ } else { /* the element was toggled closed */ } }); ``` ## [Examples](#examples) ### [A basic disclosure example](#a_basic_disclosure_example) This example shows a basic `

``` ``` details { border: 1px solid #aaaaaa; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.5em 0.5em 0; } summary { font-weight: bold; margin: -0.5em -0.5em 0; padding: 0.5em; } details[open] { padding: 0.5em; } details[open] summary { border-bottom: 1px solid #aaaaaa; margin-bottom: 0.5em; } ``` ## [Attributes](#attributes) This element includes the [global attributes](/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes). [`open`](#open) This Boolean attribute indicates whether the details — that is, the contents of the `
` element — are currently visible. The details are shown when this attribute exists, or hidden when this attribute is absent. By default this attribute is absent which means the details are not visible. **Note:** You have to remove this attribute entirely to make the details hidden. `open="false"` makes the details visible because this attribute is Boolean. [`name`](#name) This attribute enables multiple `
` elements to be connected, with only one open at a time. This allows developers to easily create UI features such as accordions without scripting. The `name` attribute specifies a group name — give multiple `
` elements the same `name` value to group them. Only one of the grouped `
` elements can be open at a time — opening one will cause another to close. If multiple grouped `
` elements are given the `open` attribute, only the first one in the source order will be rendered open. **Note:** `
` elements don't have to be adjacent to one another in the source to be part of the same group. ## [Usage notes](#usage_notes) A `
` widget can be in one of two states. The default *closed* state displays only the triangle and the label inside `` (or a [user agent](/en-US/docs/Glossary/User_agent)\-defined default string if no ``). When the user clicks on the widget or focuses it then presses the space bar, it "twists" open, revealing its contents. The common use of a triangle which rotates or twists around to represent opening or closing the widget is why these are sometimes called "twisty". You can use CSS to style the disclosure widget, and you can programmatically open and close the widget by setting/removing its [`open`](#open) attribute. Unfortunately, at this time, there's no built-in way to animate the transition between open and closed. By default when closed, the widget is only tall enough to display the disclosure triangle and summary. When open, it expands to display the details contained within. Fully standards-compliant implementations automatically apply the CSS ``[`display`](/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/display): list-item`` to the [``](/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/summary) element. ` element supports the [`toggle`](/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/toggle_event "toggle") event, which is dispatched to the `

It is sent *after* the state is changed, although if the state changes multiple times before the browser can dispatch the event, the events are coalesced so that only one is sent. You can use an event listener for the `toggle` event to detect when the widget changes state: js ``` details.addEventListener("toggle", (event) => { if (details.open) { /* the element was toggled open */ } else { /* the element was toggled closed */ } }); ``` ## [Examples](#examples) ### [A basic disclosure example](#a_basic_disclosure_example) This example shows a basic `
